title: Go module path
description: No source names the module path. The module is an application root that nothing imports from outside, so a bare module name is the narrowest choice.

title: Repeated option occurrence
description: The sources define no behavior when --target, --since, or --until appears more than once. Treating it as a usage error is the narrowest choice, since it avoids silently choosing one value.

title: Help flags
description: No source defines -h or --help. Treating them as unknown options keeps the exit-code contract complete with no extra surface.

title: Which lines register an execution_id
description: Rule 2 says a duplicate is an execution_id that appeared on an earlier line. Only kept records are counted as the first occurrence here, so a line skipped for a missing field does not block a later valid line with the same id. The sample passes under either reading.

options.label: Only kept records register an execution_id
Any JSON object line registers its execution_id

title: Invalid UTF-8 within a line
description: A line whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 cannot parse as a JSON object, so it is skipped under the malformed-line rule rather than failing the run. Only an open or read failure of the file is operational (exit 1).

title: Inverted date range
description: When --since is later than --until, no date satisfies both bounds. This follows the AC-004 precedent: the report is header-only or zero-TOTAL with exit 0, and the run is not a usage error.

title: Stub dispatch in internal/cli for the foundation step
description: Run returns usage code 2 for any report name, because no reports exist yet. Later blocks replace this with real dispatch. Should the foundation instead return a distinct code for not-yet-implemented reports?
